# @amykit/plugin-concurrent-engine

Advances one work item per tick, moving every lane of a fork at once.

A plugin for [amy](https://github.com/nicolasmelo1/amy). It provides the engine.

Use it in place of serial-engine when a workflow forks into lanes that should move together, such as ticket-to-qa running its gate and its self-review side by side. Everything else is the serial engine's, settings included: the same claim on a queue item and the same budget check before each lane's call. An install mounts one engine, so pick this one or serial-engine, with file-queue and file-store beside it.

## What it extends

|  |  |
| :-- | :-- |
| Ports | `engine` |
| Actions | _none_ |

| Events | _none_ |
| Environment | _none_ |

## Install

```sh
amy add @amykit/plugin-concurrent-engine
```

Then name it in `~/.amy/config.yaml`:

```yaml
workflows:
  your-profile:
    plugins:
      - "@amykit/plugin-concurrent-engine"
```

## Configuration

```yaml
plugins:
  "@amykit/plugin-concurrent-engine":
    maxItemAttempts: 5
    retentionDays: 7
    retryDelayMs: 300000
    staleClaimMs: 1800000
```

| Setting | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `maxItemAttempts` | `number` | no | `5` | how many times one item may fail before the operator is told and it is dropped |
| `retentionDays` | `number` | no | `7` | how long a finished queue item is kept before it is pruned |
| `retryDelayMs` | `number` | no | `300000` | how long a failed item is held before it is looked at again |
| `staleClaimMs` | `number` | no | `1800000` | how long a claimed item may sit before it counts as abandoned |

Every field is checked at boot against the schema this package declares. A key that is
not one of the above is a refusal naming the plugin and the key, not a setting that
silently never applied.
